verdict.summary: This change adds a Dockerfile that builds a sprint-metrics CLI container image from python:3.12-slim, along with tests that verify the build succeeds, the CLI runs, and the image is not architecture-pinned. The image is fit to run as a one-shot CLI (the primary and tested deployment pattern), but it runs as root, which violates the standing rule that shipped images run as a non-root user. The base image also floats rather than being pinned by digest. Neither issue prevents the image from being built or the CLI from producing correct output, but the root-privilege issue means the image runs with more privilege than it needs.

findings.concern: The image has no USER directive. The python:3.12-slim base runs as root by default, so the container executes the sprint-metrics CLI as uid 0. The tool only reads a JSON file and writes to stdout; it needs no privilege. §19 rule 8 requires that a shipped image runs as a user other than root.
findings.action: Add a non-root user after the install step. The simplest approach that keeps the acceptance criteria passing: create a virtualenv (so the install doesn't require root write to /usr/local), then drop privileges before the process runs. For example, add `RUN python -m venv /opt/venv` and `ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"` before the WORKDIR, install into the venv, then add `USER nobody` as the last line. The `nobody` user can read world-readable files (the volume-mounted cards.json will be 644) and execute the venv binary. A mechanical check: hadolint rule DL3002 (final Dockerfile has no USER) or a CI grep for `^USER` in the Dockerfile would catch this on every future change.

findings.concern: The base image `python:3.12-slim` is a floating tag. Each build pulls whatever the upstream `slim` tag currently points to, so the image is not reproducible from a clean checkout (§19 rule 7) and a base-image update can silently change the runtime. §19 rule 8 requires the base to be pinned by digest and kept current by a dependency updater.
findings.action: Pin the base by digest (e.g. `FROM python:3.12-slim@sha256:...`) and configure a dependency updater (Dependabot or Renovate) to propose digest bumps. Until the updater exists, at minimum the digest is a one-line change the author can make now. A mechanical check: a CI step that asserts the FROM line matches `@sha256:` would catch a regression to a floating tag.

findings.concern: The `--scrape` mode binds the HTTP server to 127.0.0.1 (line: `server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), MetricsHandler)`). If the image is run as a detached service with a published port (`docker run -d -p 9100:9100 ... --scrape`), the published port forwards to 0.0.0.0:9100 in the container but the server is only listening on loopback, so no external scraper can reach it. This is pre-existing code, but the image this change ships contains it.
findings.action: Bind to 0.0.0.0 when the server is intended to be reached from outside the container. A common pattern: `host = os.environ.get("BIND_ADDRESS", "127.0.0.1")` and use that in the HTTPServer constructor, then set `ENV BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0` in the Dockerfile. Alternatively, document that `--scrape` is local-only and the image's service deployment pattern is the one-shot CLI (which is what the acceptance criteria test). This does not block the change because the primary and tested deployment pattern (one-shot CLI, print to stdout, exit) is unaffected.

verdict.summary: This change adds a Dockerfile that builds the sprint-metrics CLI into a python:3.12-slim image, along with tests that build and run the image. The one-shot CLI use case works: the image can be built and the binary reached by name. However, the image violates two §19.8 requirements: it runs as root (no USER directive) and its base is a floating tag rather than a digest pin. Both are blocking because §19.8 is explicit and this image will be published to ghcr.io.

findings.concern: The Dockerfile has no USER directive. The image runs as root (uid 0), which is more privilege than the CLI needs: it reads a file argument and writes to stdout. §19.8 requires the image to run as a user other than root.
findings.action: Add a non-root user before the install step, e.g. USER 65532 (the standard _apt user that already exists in python:3.12-slim) or create a dedicated user. A mechanical check: a CI step that runs docker run --rm sprint-metrics-test id -u and asserts the output is not 0, or a hadolint rule DL3002 (final multi-stage image has a USER instruction). Note: hadolint passes a Dockerfile with no USER at all per crew#335, so the docker run id -u check is the reliable one.

findings.concern: FROM python:3.12-slim is a floating tag. The image built today is not the image built tomorrow: the base can change without a commit to this repository. §19.8 requires the base to be pinned by digest and kept current by a dependency updater. §19.7 requires every project to be reproducible.
findings.action: Replace the tag with a digest: FROM python@sha256:<digest> (run docker pull python:3.12-slim and docker inspect to get the current digest). Add a dependency-updater rule (renovate or dependabot) that updates the digest in the Dockerfile on a schedule. A mechanical check: a CI step that greps the Dockerfile for a sha256: digest in the FROM line and fails if only a tag is present.

findings.concern: The image has no ENTRYPOINT or CMD. A user must always pass the program name explicitly (docker run sprint-metrics sprint-metrics --help). §19.8 describes the pattern as docker run <image> <arguments> without repeating the program's name. However, the acceptance criteria explicitly test with the program name in the docker run command, so adding an ENTRYPOINT would break AC1 and AC2.
findings.action: Note for a follow-up story: add ENTRYPOINT ["sprint-metrics"] to the Dockerfile and update the acceptance criteria and user docs to drop the repeated program name. This is not actionable in this pull request without changing the acceptance criteria, which is the Business Analyst's domain.
findings.conflicts_with: docker run sprint-metrics-test sprint-metrics --help exits 0 with stdout containing the string sprint-metrics

findings.concern: The scrape server binds to 127.0.0.1. Inside a container, that is the container's loopback; a port mapping (-p 9100:9100) will not reach it because the kernel forwards to the container's eth0, not its lo. A user who runs docker run -p 9100:9100 sprint-metrics --scrape cannot reach the endpoint from outside the container. This is pre-existing in serve.py and not introduced or worsened by this Dockerfile change.
findings.action: Note for a follow-up: if the image is intended to be used for scraping, serve.py should bind to 0.0.0.0 (or a configurable bind address) when running in a container. The primary documented use of the image is the one-shot CLI, so this does not block the current change.

verdict.summary: This change adds a Dockerfile that builds a python:3.12-slim image with the sprint-metrics CLI installed via pip, and a test file that verifies the image builds, runs --help, and produces the expected table output from a volume-mounted cards file. The image has two blocking issues: it runs as root (violating §19.8 rule 3: "runs as a user other than root"), and it lacks an ENTRYPOINT so that docker run ghcr.io/mqucifer/sprint-metrics:1.0.0 --help starts python3 rather than the CLI (violating §19.8 rule 1: "starts the way its docs say to run it, as docker run <image> <arguments>, without repeating the program's name"). Two non-blocking notes: the base image tag floats rather than being pinned by digest (§19.8 rule 4), and the scrape server in serve.py binds to 127.0.0.1 which makes it unreachable from outside a container if the image is deployed as a long-running metrics endpoint.

findings.concern: The image runs as root. No USER directive is present, so the default from python:3.12-slim (root) applies. §19.8 rule 3 requires the image to "run as a user other than root."
findings.action: Add a USER directive after the RUN pip install line, e.g. USER 1000. The pip install runs as root (needed to write to /usr/local), but the final runtime user should be non-privileged. A hadolint check (rule DL3002) or a CI smoke test that runs docker run --rm <image> id -u and asserts the uid is non-zero would catch a regression.

findings.concern: The Dockerfile has no ENTRYPOINT or CMD directive. When the image is deployed and a user runs docker run ghcr.io/mqucifer/sprint-metrics:1.0.0 --help (the way the release docs describe: "runs the image by its tag"), the base image's default command (python3) starts, not the sprint-metrics CLI. §19.8 rule 1 requires the image to "start the way its docs say to run it, as docker run <image> <arguments>, without repeating the program's name."
findings.action: Add ENTRYPOINT ["sprint-metrics"] to the Dockerfile. Update tests/test_dockerfile.py to invoke docker run --rm sprint-metrics-test --help (without the program name) so the test proves the image works the way it will be run in production. This conflicts with the current acceptance criterion wording but is the form §19.8 requires; the story's criteria should be updated to match.
findings.conflicts_with: docker run sprint-metrics-test sprint-metrics --help exits 0 with stdout containing the string sprint-metrics

findings.concern: The base image python:3.12-slim is a floating tag. §19.8 rule 4 requires the image to be "built from a base pinned by digest, kept current by a dependency updater." A floating tag means the image is not reproducible: a rebuild tomorrow may pull a different base.
findings.action: Pin the base by digest (python:3.12-slim@sha256:...) and configure a dependency updater (Renovate or Dependabot) to propose digest updates on a schedule. This can be addressed before the first release rather than in this PR, but the Dockerfile should not be published with a floating base.

findings.concern: The scrape HTTP server binds to 127.0.0.1 (line: server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), MetricsHandler)). In a container, Docker port publishing forwards traffic to the container's eth0 IP, not loopback, so a user who runs docker run -p 9100:9100 ghcr.io/mqucifer/sprint-metrics:1.0.0 /cards.json --scrape --port 9100 will not be able to reach the /metrics endpoint from the host or from a Prometheus scraper.
findings.action: Bind to 0.0.0.0 instead of 127.0.0.1 (or make it configurable via an environment variable). A CI smoke test that runs the image with --scrape and a published port, then curls the /metrics endpoint from the host, would prove reachability. This is a note because the image's primary use is as a one-shot CLI; the scrape mode is secondary and its 127.0.0.1 binding may be intentional for local development.

verdict.summary: This change adds a Dockerfile that installs the sprint-metrics CLI into a python:3.12-slim image, plus tests that verify the image builds, responds to --help, and produces correct output for a sample cards file when run with a volume mount. The image is buildable and runnable for its tested use cases (batch CLI mode). However, it runs as root, which is more privilege than the CLI needs, violating §19.8's requirement that the image 'runs as a user other than root.' This is a blocking finding. Additionally, the base image is not pinned by digest (a §19.8 requirement), and the --scrape mode's 127.0.0.1 binding would make it unreachable from outside the container—neither of which blocks this change but both should be addressed.

findings.concern: The Dockerfile has no USER directive. The python:3.12-slim base image defaults to running as root (UID 0). The sprint-metrics CLI only reads files and writes to stdout; it does not need root. §19.8 requires that an image 'runs as a user other than root,' and the deploy review blocks an image that 'runs with more privilege than it needs.'
findings.action: Add a USER directive after the pip install step, e.g. create a non-root user (or use the existing 'nobody' user) and switch to it before the install or at the end. A mechanical check: a CI step (or a hadolint rule DL3002, which flags images without a USER instruction) run on the Dockerfile would catch this. The project's own smoke test should assert `id -u` returns non-zero inside the running container.

findings.concern: FROM python:3.12-slim uses a mutable tag. A rebuild at a later date could pull a different base image, making builds non-reproducible. §19.8 requires the image 'is built from a base pinned by digest, kept current by a dependency updater.'
findings.action: Pin the base image by its SHA256 digest (e.g. FROM python:3.12-slim@sha256:...). Add a dependency updater (such as a GitHub Action using a tool like `renovate` or `depsbot`, or a manual process) that proposes updates when a new digest is published for the same tag. This is a note for this change but should be resolved before the first release is cut.

findings.concern: The scrape HTTP server binds to 127.0.0.1 (line: `http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), MetricsHandler)`). When the container is run with `docker run -p 9100:9100 ... sprint-metrics --scrape cards.json`, the published port maps to the container's network namespace, but the server only listens on the container's loopback. No external process can reach /metrics. This does not affect the batch-mode use cases tested by the acceptance criteria, but it does affect the --scrape mode when the image is the deployment vehicle.
findings.action: Make the bind address configurable, e.g. via an environment variable (SPRINT_METRICS_BIND, default 127.0.0.1 for bare-metal use) so a container deployment can set it to 0.0.0.0. This is in older code (serve.py) and does not block this Dockerfile change, but it should be tracked so the image's scrape mode is actually reachable when deployed as a service. A smoke test that starts the container detached with its port published and curls /metrics from the host would catch this.

verdict.summary: This change adds a Dockerfile that builds the sprint-metrics CLI into a minimal Python 3.12 image, plus a test file that verifies the build succeeds, the CLI runs, and no architecture-specific substrings appear. The image is fit to run the CLI use case (the acceptance criteria's primary target), but it has two gaps against §19.8: it runs as root (no USER directive), and the base image is not pinned by digest. Both are blocking for an image the release workflow will publish to ghcr.io. A pre-existing issue in serve.py (binding to 127.0.0.1) makes the optional --scrape mode unreachable from outside the container when port-published, but that does not touch the primary CLI deployment this story delivers.

findings.concern: No USER directive. The python:3.12-slim base image runs as root (uid 0) by default, and nothing in this Dockerfile creates or switches to a non-root user. §19.8 requires that an image the crew publishes 'runs as a user other than root.'
findings.action: Add a USER directive. Create a non-root user (e.g. `RUN useradd --create-home appuser` or use the `adduser` available in Debian-based images) and set `USER appuser` before the install step so the installed application runs unprivileged. A smoke test that runs `docker run --rm <image> id -u` and asserts the output is not `0` would catch a regression: add it to the project's CI alongside the existing build-and-run test in tests/test_dockerfile.py.

findings.concern: `FROM python:3.12-slim` uses a floating tag. §19.8 requires that an image the crew publishes 'is built from a base pinned by digest, kept current by a dependency updater.' A floating tag means the build is not reproducible (§19.7): two builds on different days can pull different base layers, and there is no mechanism to alert when the upstream tag moves.
findings.action: Pin the base by digest: `FROM python:3.12-slim@sha256:<digest>` (resolve the current digest with `docker manifest inspect python:3.12-slim`). Add a dependency updater (Renovate, Dependabot with container support, or Trivy in CI) that opens a PR when the digest for python:3.12-slim changes, so the pin stays current without manual intervention. The existing test in tests/test_dockerfile.py already builds the image, so a digest change will be validated by CI on the updater's PR.

findings.concern: The HTTP server binds to `127.0.0.1` (line: `http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), ...)`). When the image is run with `docker run -p 9100:9100 ... --scrape`, Docker's port forward targets the container's default interface, not loopback, so the scrape endpoint is unreachable from outside the container. This is a pre-existing issue in the code, not introduced by this Dockerfile, but the image ships this code and the release process will publish it to ghcr.io.
findings.action: This is a note, not a blocker for this story, because the primary deployment mode is the CLI (run-and-exit) and the acceptance criteria do not cover --scrape. When a story addresses the scrape use case in a container, change the bind address to `0.0.0.0` (or make it configurable via an environment variable) and add a test that starts the server with a published port and curls it from the host. Until then, document that --scrape inside a container requires `--network host` or a code change.

verdict.summary: This change adds a Dockerfile that builds the sprint-metrics CLI into a container image from python:3.12-slim, along with tests that verify the build, the --help output, a sample run with cards.json, and the absence of architecture-specific strings. The primary use case (one-shot CLI invocation) works as documented. However, the image runs as root (no USER directive) and the base image is a floating tag rather than a digest, both of which violate §19.8's requirements for what ships as an image. These are blocking.

findings.concern: The Dockerfile has no USER directive. python:3.12-slim defaults to root, so the image runs as UID 0. The sprint-metrics tool reads JSON files and writes to stdout; it requires no privilege. §19.8 requires that an image 'runs as a user other than root,' and this image runs with more privilege than it needs.
findings.action: Add a non-root user and set the USER before the final install or at minimum before the image is used. For example, create a user with `RUN useradd --create-home appuser` and add `USER appuser` after the install step (or before, adjusting WORKDIR ownership). A mechanical check that would catch this: a hadolint rule (DL3002) flags images without a USER instruction, or a smoke test in CI that runs `docker run --rm <image> id -u` and asserts the result is not 0.

findings.concern: FROM python:3.12-slim uses a floating tag. The base image can change at any time without notice, breaking reproducibility. §19.8 requires the image 'is built from a base pinned by digest, kept current by a dependency updater.'
findings.action: Pin the base image to a digest: `FROM python:3.12-slim@sha256:<digest>`. Configure a dependency updater (Dependabot with a `docker` ecosystem entry, or a similar tool) to propose digest updates on a schedule. The updater is the mechanism that keeps the pin current; the digest is what makes the build reproducible.

findings.concern: There is no .dockerignore file. The build context sent to the Docker daemon includes the entire working directory (.git, tests/, .github/, etc.). This increases context upload time and the risk that sensitive files (e.g., .env, credentials) are accidentally included in a build layer if a future COPY instruction broadens its scope.
findings.action: Add a .dockerignore at the repository root excluding at minimum: `.git`, `tests/`, `.github/`, `*.md` (other than README.md which is explicitly COPY'd), and any files not needed for the build. This is hygiene, not a correctness issue for the current image, but it protects against a future COPY . mistake.

verdict.summary: This change adds a Dockerfile that builds the sprint-metrics CLI into a container image, plus a test file that proves the image builds, runs `sprint-metrics --help`, and produces the expected output for a sample cards file. The Dockerfile is not architecture-pinned (AC3), and the tests cover all three acceptance criteria. However, the image as written runs as root and uses a floating base-image tag, both of which violate §19.8 requirements for what ships as an image. Two blocking findings.

findings.concern: The image has no USER directive. The python:3.12-slim base image defaults to root, so every process in the container—including the sprint-metrics CLI and any `--scrape` HTTP server—runs as root. §19.8 requires that an image 'runs as a user other than root.'
findings.action: Add a non-root user before the RUN step. For example: `RUN useradd -m appuser` then `USER appuser` (or use the `USER` directive after a `RUN useradd` to create a user with no password). The installed package lives in /usr/local/bin and /usr/local/lib, both world-readable, so no further permission setup is needed for the CLI use case. A smoke test that asserts the container's effective uid is non-zero (e.g., `docker run image id -u` and check the output) would catch this mechanically next time; hadolint rule SC1091 does not apply here, but a `docker run --rm image id` check in CI would.

findings.concern: The base image `python:3.12-slim` is a floating tag. Its content changes whenever the upstream publishes a new 3.12-slim build, making the image non-reproducible. §19.8 requires the image 'is built from a base pinned by digest, kept current by a dependency updater.'
findings.action: Pin the base by digest: `FROM python@sha256:<full-digest>`. The digest can be obtained from `docker manifest inspect python:3.12-slim` or from the GHCR/Docker Hub API. Add a Dependabot or Renovate configuration to update the digest periodically. A mechanical check: a CI step that verifies the FROM line contains `@sha256:` and rejects bare tags (a simple grep in the release workflow, or a custom action). No existing linter rule catches this; hadolint does not flag unpinned tags.

findings.concern: No .dockerignore file accompanies the Dockerfile. The build context sent to the Docker daemon includes the entire repository (tests/, .git/, etc.), making builds slower and risking accidental inclusion of sensitive files if the COPY commands ever change to `COPY . .`.
findings.action: Add a `.dockerignore` at the repository root excluding at minimum: `.git/`, `tests/`, `.github/`, `*.md` (except README.md which is explicitly COPY'd), and `__pycache__/`. This is a hardening measure, not a correctness issue, so it does not block the merge.

findings.concern: The `--scrape` HTTP server binds to `127.0.0.1` (line: `http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), ...)`). Inside a container, this address is only reachable from within the container itself; a host-side Prometheus or any sidecar cannot scrape it. This is a pre-existing application design choice, not introduced by this Dockerfile, but it means the `--scrape` mode is effectively unusable when the tool runs in a container.
findings.action: Note for a future story: if containerised scraping is a supported use case, the bind address should be configurable (e.g., an environment variable or a `--host` flag) so it can be set to `0.0.0.0` inside a container. This does not block the current change, which ships a CLI tool whose primary interface is file input/output.

verdict.summary: The change adds a Dockerfile that packages the sprint-metrics CLI into a python:3.12-slim image, along with tests that build and exercise the image. The CLI use case works: the image builds, the console script is invocable, and the card-file input path functions. However, four issues prevent the image from meeting §19 rule 8 as deployed: it runs as root (no USER directive), the base image is a floating tag rather than a digest, there is no ENTRYPOINT so the caller must repeat the program name, and the scrape server in serve.py binds to 127.0.0.1 making it unreachable from outside the container when a port is published.

findings.concern: The Dockerfile has no USER directive. The python:3.12-slim base image runs as root by default, so the entire container process (pip install and the resulting sprint-metrics invocation) executes with UID 0. §19 rule 8 requires the image to 'run as a user other than root.' A CLI tool that reads a JSON file and writes to stdout has no need for root.
findings.action: Add a USER directive. Since the package is installed to /usr/local (writable only by root at build time), the runtime user needs read access to /usr/local/lib and /usr/local/bin, which the default permissions provide. Add `USER 1000` (or create a named user with `RUN useradd -m appuser && USER appuser`) after the RUN pip install line. A mechanical check: a hadolint rule (DL3002) flags images with no USER directive; adding it to the CI lint step on Dockerfiles would catch this next time. The CI smoke test (§19 rule 8) should assert the running user is not root: `docker run --rm sprint-metrics-test id -u` should print a non-zero value.

findings.concern: The base image is `FROM python:3.12-slim`, a floating tag. The digest behind this tag changes upstream without notice, so a rebuild at a later date may pull a different (potentially broken or compromised) base. §19 rule 8 requires the image to be 'built from a base pinned by digest, kept current by a dependency updater.'
findings.action: Pin the base image by digest: `FROM python:3.12-slim@sha256:<current-digest>`. Obtain the digest with `docker manifest inspect python:3.12-slim` or `crane manifest python:3.12-slim`. Add a dependency updater (Dependabot with the `docker` ecosystem, or Renovate) to the repository configuration so the digest is refreshed on a schedule. A mechanical check: a CI step that parses the Dockerfile and asserts the FROM line contains `@sha256:` would catch a regression to a floating tag.

findings.concern: The Dockerfile sets no ENTRYPOINT or CMD. The only way to invoke the tool is `docker run <image> sprint-metrics <args>`, repeating the program name as a container argument. §19 rule 8 requires the image to start 'as `docker run <image> <arguments>`, without repeating the program's name,' and the CI proof must demonstrate this form.
findings.action: Add `ENTRYPOINT ["sprint-metrics"]` to the Dockerfile. This makes `docker run <image> --help` and `docker run <image> /input/cards.json` work directly, satisfying §19 rule 8. The acceptance criteria and the tests in this PR must be updated to drop the redundant `sprint-metrics` argument from the docker run invocations (e.g., `docker run sprint-metrics-test --help` instead of `docker run sprint-metrics-test sprint-metrics --help`).
findings.conflicts_with: Given the repository in its current state with pyproject.toml defining the sprint-metrics console script and src/sprint_metrics/ containing the package When docker build -t sprint-metrics-test . is executed from the repository root Then the build exits 0 and docker run sprint-metrics-test sprint-metrics --help exits 0 with stdout containing the string sprint-metrics

findings.concern: The scrape HTTP server binds to 127.0.0.1 (line: `http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), MetricsHandler)`). Inside a container, 127.0.0.1 is the container's loopback interface; no traffic from outside the container (including a host that has published the port) can reach it. §19 rule 8 requires that a service 'is started detached with its port published, and answers from outside the container.' A user running `docker run -d -p 9100:9100 <image> --scrape` gets a server that no external Prometheus scraper can contact.
findings.action: Change the bind address to `0.0.0.0` (or introduce an environment variable such as `SPRINT_METRICS_BIND` defaulting to `0.0.0.0` so local non-container use can still opt into loopback-only binding). The mechanical check that would catch this next time is the §19 rule 8 CI smoke test: start the container detached with its port published, then curl the port from the host and assert a 200 response with the expected Prometheus text. A test that merely checks the server started (as the current code does by printing the port) would pass even with the loopback bind.

Per §19.8, what ships as an image must run as a user other than root. The base image is also not pinned by digest, which §19.8 requires, though this doesn't prevent the image from building or running.

findings.concern: The Dockerfile has no USER directive. The python:3.12-slim base image runs as root by default, so the container process runs as root. The sprint-metrics CLI reads a JSON file and prints a report (or serves on port 9100, which is unprivileged). It does not need root.
findings.action: Add a USER directive before the final RUN or after it, e.g. USER 65534 (nobody). §19.8 requires the image to run as a user other than root. A smoke test that does docker run and checks the effective uid (e.g. asserting the output of id -u is not 0) would catch a regression. hadolint does not catch a missing USER, so this needs a dedicated check in the project's CI.

findings.concern: The base image python:3.12-slim is a floating tag, not a digest. §19.8 requires the image to be built from a base pinned by digest, kept current by a dependency updater. As written, a rebuild of this Dockerfile could pull a different base than the one that was tested and shipped.

This is hardening that doesn't stop the image from working, so it is a note rather than a blocker for this PR — but it should be addressed before the first release is published.

findings.concern: pip install --no-cache-dir . resolves dependencies at build time from PyPI. There is no lockfile copied into the build context, so the exact dependency versions that end up in the image are not reproducible from the repository alone. §19.3 requires dependencies to be locked with a lockfile.
findings.action: Generate a lockfile from pyproject.toml (e.g. uv pip compile pyproject.toml > requirements.txt or use uv export), copy it into the Dockerfile, and install from it (pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt or the equivalent for the project's package manager). A check in CI that the lockfile is in sync with pyproject.toml would catch drift.

verdict.summary: This change adds a Dockerfile that builds the sprint-metrics CLI into a python:3.12-slim image, along with tests that verify the build succeeds and the CLI runs as expected. The image is reached by `docker run <image> sprint-metrics <args>`, runs as root with no USER directive, and uses a floating base tag. It cannot be approved as-is because §19.8 requires the image to run as a user other than root, and this Dockerfile gives the container the full privilege of a CLI tool that only reads a file and writes to stdout.

findings.concern: The Dockerfile has no USER directive. The python:3.12-slim base image runs as root by default, so `docker run sprint-metrics-test sprint-metrics --help` executes as uid 0. A CLI that reads a JSON file and prints a table to stdout requires no privilege.
findings.action: Add a USER directive after the pip install, e.g. `USER nobody` (the user python:3.12-slim already creates for non-root work). The working directory /app must be readable by that user; since the files are copied with default permissions they will be. Verify with `docker run sprint-metrics-test id` that the output shows `uid=65534(nobody)`. §19.8 requires the image to run as a user other than root; a hadolint run with the `USER` check would catch a missing directive next time, but the definitive proof is the smoke test that AC1 and AC2 already provide.

findings.concern: The base image is referenced by a floating tag (`python:3.12-slim`), not by digest. §19.8 requires the image to be 'built from a base pinned by digest, kept current by a dependency updater.' A build today and a build next month may pull different base layers, making the released image non-reproducible.
findings.action: Pin the base by digest: `FROM python:3.12-slim@sha256:<digest>`. Add a Dependabot or Renovate configuration that updates the digest on a schedule so the image stays current without manual intervention. This does not conflict with any acceptance criterion; the arch-agnostic check (AC3) only forbids architecture substrings and is unaffected by a digest suffix.

verdict.summary: This change adds a Dockerfile that builds a sprint-metrics CLI container image from python:3.12-slim, plus tests that verify the build, CLI invocation, and architecture neutrality. The image is not fit to run as deployed: it runs as root (violating §19.8), it has no ENTRYPOINT so the program name must be repeated on every invocation (violating §19.8's requirement that the image be proven as `docker run <image> <arguments>` without repeating the program's name), and the base image floats on a tag rather than being pinned by digest (§19.8). Two of these are blocking.

findings.concern: The image has no USER directive. The python:3.12-slim base image defaults to root, so every process in the container runs as root. §19.8 requires the image to 'run as a user other than root.'
findings.action: Add a non-root user and set USER before the final install or at the end. For example: `RUN useradd --create-home --uid 1000 appuser` followed by `USER appuser`. A mechanical check that would catch this: a smoke test in CI that runs `docker run --rm <image> id -u` and asserts the result is not 0, or a hadolint rule DL3002 (final stage is root). The deploy review (§20) checks this on every change that ships an image.

findings.concern: The image has no ENTRYPOINT. §19.8 requires that the image be proven in CI 'as `docker run <image> <arguments>`, without repeating the program's name.' Without an ENTRYPOINT, every invocation must repeat `sprint-metrics` as the first argument (e.g. `docker run image sprint-metrics --help`), which is not the form §19.8 prescribes.
findings.action: Add `ENTRYPOINT ["sprint-metrics"]` to the Dockerfile. Then update AC1 and AC2 in the story (and the corresponding test assertions in tests/test_dockerfile.py) to invoke the image without repeating the program name: `docker run --rm sprint-metrics-test --help` and `docker run --rm -v ... sprint-metrics-test /input/cards.json`. The mechanical check is the smoke test in CI itself: a test that runs `docker run --rm <image> --help` and asserts exit 0, which only passes once the ENTRYPOINT is set.
findings.conflicts_with: Given the repository in its current state with pyproject.toml defining the sprint-metrics console script and src/sprint_metrics/ containing the package When docker build -t sprint-metrics-test . is executed from the repository root Then the build exits 0 and docker run sprint-metrics-test sprint-metrics --help exits 0 with stdout containing the string sprint-metrics

findings.concern: The base image is `python:3.12-slim`, a floating tag. §19.8 requires the image to be 'built from a base pinned by digest, kept current by a dependency updater.' A floating tag means the build is not reproducible: the same Dockerfile can produce different images on different days as the 3.12 patch level advances.
findings.action: Replace `python:3.12-slim` with the fully qualified digest, e.g. `python@sha256:<digest>`. Add the image to a dependency updater (Dependabot or Renovate) configured to update the digest on a schedule. The mechanical check: a CI step (or a pre-commit hook) that fails if the FROM line does not end in a `@sha256:` digest. The deploy review (§20) checks this on every change that ships an image.

findings.concern: The scrape server binds to 127.0.0.1 (`http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), ...)`). When the container image is deployed with a published port (e.g. `docker run -p 9100:9100`), the server is unreachable from outside the container because it only listens on the loopback interface inside the container's network namespace. §19.8 requires that a service 'is reached the way a user reaches it: a service is started detached with its port published, and answers from outside the container.'
findings.action: This is existing code outside this story's scope (the story covers the CLI, not the scrape mode). When a future story deploys the scrape mode, change the bind address to `0.0.0.0` (or make it configurable via an environment variable) so the server is reachable through a published port. A smoke test that starts the container detached with `-p` and curls the port from the host would catch this.

verdict.summary: This change adds a Dockerfile that builds a minimal Python 3.12 image with the sprint-metrics CLI installed, plus a test file that verifies the build, the --help output, a volume-mounted cards.json run, and the absence of architecture pinning. The image is fit for its primary use case (one-shot CLI: read a file, print a report). However, the image also ships the --scrape mode, which binds to 127.0.0.1 in serve.py and therefore cannot be reached from outside the container when the image is deployed as a Prometheus scrape target. One blocking finding, two notes.

findings.concern: The HTTPServer binds to ("127.0.0.1", port) on line 49. The Dockerfile ships this code into an image that the release process publishes to ghcr.io and that the crew runs by tag. When a user runs docker run -p 9100:9100 ghcr.io/mqucifer/sprint-metrics:1.0.0 sprint-metrics --scrape --cards /input/cards.json, the container's port-forwarding is useless because the server is not listening on the container's external interface. The --scrape mode cannot be reached as deployed.
findings.action: Change the bind address to "0.0.0.0" (or accept it as a parameter with 0.0.0.0 as the default) so the scrape endpoint is reachable from outside the container. Add a smoke test to tests/test_dockerfile.py that builds the image, runs it with --scrape and a known cards file, and asserts that a second subprocess (simulating an external scraper) can curl the /metrics endpoint on the published port and receive a 200 with the expected metric names. This is the check that would catch a regression to 127.0.0.1 next time.

findings.concern: The image has no USER directive and inherits the root user from python:3.12-slim. The tool only reads a volume-mounted JSON file and writes to stdout; it does not need root. Running as root is more privilege than the workload requires.
findings.action: Add a USER directive (e.g. USER nosuchuser or a dedicated uid like 65532) after the pip install step. This is a hardening measure; it does not stop the tool working, so it is a note rather than a blocker. If the crew wants a mechanical guard, a lint rule (hadolint DL3002) on the Dockerfile in CI would flag a missing USER directive.

findings.concern: FROM python:3.12-slim uses a mutable tag. Two builds on different days may pull different base images, making the image non-reproducible. §19.7 requires every project to be reproducible from a clean checkout.
findings.action: Pin the base image to a digest (e.g. FROM python:3.12-slim@sha256:…) or at minimum to a specific patch version (python:3.12.7-slim). A digest is preferable because even a patch-version tag is mutable. The release workflow that builds and pushes the image should use the pinned reference so that the published image is bit-for-bit reproducible. A CI check (e.g. a step that asserts the FROM line contains a digest, or a hadolint rule DL3007) would catch a regression to a floating tag.

verdict.summary: This change adds a Dockerfile that installs the sprint-metrics CLI into a python:3.12-slim image, plus tests that verify the build and a sample run. The image is fit to build and run: the console script installs cleanly, the tool reads from a volume-mounted file and writes to stdout, and the --scrape server binds to 127.0.0.1 only. However, the Dockerfile contains no USER directive, so the container runs as root. The tool only needs to read a file and write to stdout — it requires zero privilege — and the deploy review blocks when what ships runs with more privilege than it needs.

findings.concern: The Dockerfile has no USER directive. The base image python:3.12-slim defaults to root, so the container runs as root. The sprint-metrics tool only reads a JSON file from a volume mount and writes to stdout (or serves on 127.0.0.1:9100 via --scrape). None of these operations require root privilege.
findings.action: Add a non-root user after the pip install step, e.g. `USER nobody` or create a dedicated user with `RUN useradd -r sprint && USER sprint`. The installed packages in /usr/local/lib are world-readable by default, and volume-mounted files in the test are created with mode 644, so readability is not affected. This does not conflict with any acceptance criterion: AC1 runs --help (no file I/O) and AC2 mounts a world-readable file.

findings.concern: The base image `python:3.12-slim` floats on the patch level (it tracks the latest 3.12.x). Dependencies are installed via `pip install --no-cache-dir .` which resolves at build time; the project's uv.lock is not copied or used. This means the image is not bit-for-bit reproducible from a clean checkout.
findings.action: This is a note, not a blocker. For full reproducibility per §19.7, consider pinning the base to a digest (e.g. `python@sha256:...`) or at least a patch tag (`python:3.12.5-slim`), and copying the lockfile with `COPY uv.lock ./` then installing with `uv pip install --system .` or `pip install --require-hashes -r uv.lock`. A dependency updater (e.g. a Renovate or Dependabot rule for the base image tag) would catch stale pins.

verdict.summary: This change adds a Dockerfile that installs the sprint-metrics package into a python:3.12-slim image, plus tests that build and run it. The image is fit for its primary CLI use case (reading a cards file, printing a table to stdout). However, it ships a scrape server (serve.py) that binds to 127.0.0.1, making that endpoint unreachable from outside the container, and it runs as root when the tool only needs to read a file and write to stdout. Two findings block; one notes a reproducibility gap.

findings.concern: The scrape server binds to 127.0.0.1 (line: `server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), MetricsHandler)`). The Dockerfile ships this code into the image. When the container is deployed and `sprint-metrics --scrape` is invoked, the server listens only on the container's internal loopback. No external process (a host Prometheus, a sidecar, an orchestrator) can reach it. The endpoint is unreachable as deployed.
findings.action: Bind to 0.0.0.0 so the server is reachable through the container's published port. Change the bind address to `0.0.0.0` (or make it configurable via an environment variable such as `BIND_ADDRESS` with a default of `0.0.0.0` when running in a container). Add `EXPOSE 9100` to the Dockerfile to document the port. A smoke test that runs the image with `--scrape` and curls the published port from the host would catch a regression: `docker run -d -p 9100:9100 sprint-metrics-test sprint-metrics --scrape` followed by `curl -sf http://localhost:9100/metrics`.

findings.concern: No USER directive. The python:3.12-slim base image runs as root (uid 0). The sprint-metrics CLI reads a JSON file and writes to stdout; it does not bind to privileged ports, write system files, or require any root capability. The container runs with more privilege than the tool needs.
findings.action: Add a non-root user. After the pip install step, add: `RUN useradd --create-home appuser && chown -R appuser /app` then `USER appuser`. This ensures the process runs unprivileged. A CI check (or a linter such as hadolint rule DL3002) flags a Dockerfile with no USER directive after any RUN step that creates a user.

findings.concern: The build context copies pyproject.toml and src/ but no lockfile. `pip install --no-cache-dir .` resolves dependencies from PyPI at build time, so two builds at different times can pull different dependency versions. This violates §19.7 (every project is reproducible) and §19.3 (dependencies are locked with a lockfile).
findings.action: Copy the project's lockfile (uv.lock or equivalent) into the build context and use it for installation. For a uv-based project: `COPY uv.lock pyproject.toml README.md ./` then `RUN uv pip install --system .` (or `pip install --no-cache-dir -r uv.lock .` if using pip). This pins the exact dependency versions at build time.

verdict.summary: This change adds a Dockerfile that builds a minimal Python 3.12 image with the sprint-metrics CLI installed via pip, plus a test file that verifies the build, the --help output, a real invocation with a volume-mounted cards file, and the absence of architecture-specific substrings. The image is a straightforward CLI container: it reads a JSON file, computes metrics, prints a table, and exits. It can be run as deployed (docker run by tag, invoking the console script) and the scrape server binds to 127.0.0.1 so it is not reachable from outside the container. However, the image runs as root, which is more privilege than this read-and-print CLI needs. That is blocking.

findings.concern: The image runs as root. The python:3.12-slim base image has no USER directive by default, and this Dockerfile adds none. The sprint-metrics CLI only reads a file (from a volume mount or stdin) and writes to stdout; it needs no elevated privilege. A container that can read /etc/shadow, write to /etc, or access the host's device files via a volume mount is running with more privilege than it needs.
findings.action: Add a USER directive after the pip install step. The python:3.12-slim image ships a 'python' user (uid 1000) that can read the installed packages in /usr/local/lib and execute the console script in /usr/local/bin. Add 'USER python' as the final line of the Dockerfile. Verify with: docker run --rm sprint-metrics-test sprint-metrics --help (should still exit 0), and docker run --rm sprint-metrics-test id (should show uid=1000(python)).

findings.concern: The base image tag python:3.12-slim floats: it tracks the latest 3.12.x patch release from the Docker Hub. A build today and a build next month can pull different underlying packages (glibc, OpenSSL, Python patch level) without any change to the Dockerfile. The project's release process (§19.7) requires reproducibility: a build from a clean checkout produces the same artifact. The same concern applies to pip install . resolving dependencies to the latest compatible versions at build time, since no lockfile is copied into the image.
findings.action: Pin the base image to a digest (e.g. FROM python:3.12-slim@sha256:...) or to a specific patch tag (python:3.12.5-slim), and copy a uv.lock or requirements.txt with pinned hashes into the image so pip installs exact versions. This can be addressed in a follow-up card; it does not prevent the current image from building and running. A CI step that checks the base image tag is a digest or a fully-qualified version (not a minor-only tag) would catch this next time: a grep or a Dockerfile linter rule (hadolint DL3007) flags floating tags.

verdict.summary: This change adds a Dockerfile that builds the sprint-metrics CLI into a python:3.12-slim image, plus a test file that verifies the image builds, the CLI responds to --help, and a known cards.json input produces the expected table row. The image is intended to be built for both linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 (no architecture pin in the Dockerfile, confirmed by test). The CI tests.yml workflow will run the new tests on every PR. The image is fit to run: the CLI is reached by docker run with the console-script entry point, the scrape mode binds to 127.0.0.1 on an unprivileged port, and the build is not architecture-pinned. However, the container runs as root when it does not need to, which is more privilege than the workload requires and blocks the change under §20.

findings.concern: No USER directive is present. The python:3.12-slim base image defaults to root. The sprint-metrics CLI reads a JSON file from a volume mount and writes to stdout; the optional scrape server binds to 127.0.0.1 on port 9100 (or an ephemeral port, both above 1024). No part of the workload requires root: no privileged port, no sysctl, no device access, no filesystem operation outside the volume mount and stdout.
findings.action: Add a USER directive after the RUN pip install step. For example: create a dedicated user (RUN useradd --create-home --uid 1000 appuser && USER appuser) or use the existing nobody user (USER nobody). The directory /app is owned by root after pip install, so either chown it to the new user before the USER switch, or install into a path the user can read (e.g., the system site-packages, which is world-readable). A mechanical check: hadolint rule DL3002 flags images that lack a USER instruction; add it to the project's CI lint step or to a future Dockerfile lint job.

findings.concern: pip install --no-cache-dir . resolves dependencies from PyPI at build time rather than installing from the project's lockfile. §19.3 requires dependencies to be locked. Two builds from the same source on different days may pull different dependency versions, making the image non-reproducible.
findings.action: Copy the lockfile into the build context and install from it. For example: COPY uv.lock ./ then use uv pip install --system . (uv respects the lockfile by default), or generate a requirements.txt with exact pins from the lock and use pip install --no-cache-dir --require-hashes -r requirements.txt. This makes the image bit-reproducible given the same source and base image.

findings.concern: No .dockerignore file is present in the diff. COPY src/ ./src/ will include any __pycache__ directories, .pyc files, or test fixtures that exist under src/ in the build context. This bloats the image and may include files that serve no purpose at runtime.
findings.action: Add a .dockerignore file at the repository root excluding at minimum __pycache__, *.pyc, .git, and any test fixture directories under src/. This is a hygiene and image-size concern; it does not affect whether the image runs correctly.
